explain.es: Una participle clause es una oración subordinada sin sujeto y sin conector, construida con un participio: -ing (present participle), participio pasado (-ed o 3.ª columna) o having + participio (perfect participle). Sustituye a oraciones con because, as, when, after, if, so o who / which, y hace el texto más conciso y formal. La regla de oro: el sujeto implícito del participio tiene que ser el mismo que el de la oración principal.
explain.en: A participle clause has no subject and no conjunction. It replaces clauses with because, when, after, if, so or who / which, making writing concise and formal. Its implied subject must be the subject of the main clause.
formula: As she felt tired, she went home. (neutra)

explain.title: 1 · -ing: tiempo
explain.es: Con -ing el sentido es activo: el sujeto hace la acción. Expresa una acción simultánea (= while, as) o inmediatamente anterior (= when, as soon as) a la principal. En español solemos usar al + infinitivo o un gerundio: Al abrir la puerta… / Paseando por…
explain.en: -ing = active meaning. It expresses a simultaneous action (= while) or one immediately before the main action (= when, as soon as).

examples.en: Opening the report, the director noticed a serious error.
examples.es: Al abrir el informe, la directora detectó un error grave.

examples.en: Walking through the old town, we came across a small bookshop.
examples.es: Paseando por el casco antiguo, nos topamos con una pequeña librería.

examples.en: Hearing the fire alarm, the staff left the building immediately.
examples.es: Al oír la alarma de incendios, el personal salió del edificio inmediatamente.

explain.title: 2 · -ing: causa y resultado
explain.es: Causa (= because, as, since): muy frecuente con verbos de estado como being, knowing, feeling, realising, wanting, having. Resultado (= and so, and as a result): la participial va al final, tras una coma, y su sujeto lógico es toda la oración anterior: …, causing delays, …, leaving thousands without power. Es un recurso típico de las noticias.
explain.en: Reason: Being / Knowing / Feeling… at the start. Result: …, causing / leaving / making… at the end, after a comma.

examples.en: Being the most experienced member of the team, Laura was asked to lead the project.
examples.es: Al ser la integrante con más experiencia del equipo, a Laura le pidieron que dirigiera el proyecto.

examples.en: Knowing how competitive the market was, they lowered their prices.
examples.es: Sabiendo lo competitivo que era el mercado, bajaron los precios.

examples.en: The storm brought down power lines, leaving thousands of homes without electricity.
examples.es: La tormenta derribó tendidos eléctricos y dejó a miles de hogares sin luz.

explain.title: 3 · Participio pasado: pasiva
explain.es: Con el participio pasado el sentido es pasivo: el sujeto recibe la acción. Puede expresar causa, tiempo o condición (= if): Used correctly… = If it is used correctly… Funciona como el participio español: Construido en 1890…, Bien utilizado…, Conmocionado por…
explain.en: Past participle = passive meaning: the subject receives the action. It can express reason, time or condition (= if).

examples.en: Built in 1890, the bridge is now a protected monument.
examples.es: Construido en 1890, el puente es hoy un monumento protegido.

examples.en: Used correctly, this software can save hours of work.
examples.es: Bien utilizado, este programa puede ahorrar horas de trabajo.

examples.en: Shocked by the results, the board called an emergency meeting.
examples.es: Conmocionado por los resultados, el consejo convocó una reunión de urgencia.

explain.title: 4 · Having + participio
explain.es: El perfect participle indica que una acción terminó antes que la principal y, a menudo, que es su causa. Activa: having + participio (Having finished…); pasiva: having been + participio (Having been warned…). Es necesario cuando la primera acción duró un tiempo o cuando sin él la secuencia quedaría confusa: Having lived in Japan for ten years, she speaks fluent Japanese.
explain.en: Having + past participle = an action completed before the main one (often its cause). Passive: having been + past participle.

examples.en: Having finished the presentation, she answered questions from the audience.
examples.es: Tras terminar la presentación, respondió a las preguntas del público.

examples.en: Having lived abroad for ten years, he found it hard to readapt.
examples.es: Después de haber vivido diez años en el extranjero, le costó readaptarse.

examples.en: Having been warned about the risks, the investors withdrew.
examples.es: Tras haber sido advertidos de los riesgos, los inversores se retiraron.

explain.title: 5 · Negativa y conjunción + participio
explain.es: La negativa se forma con not delante del participio: Not knowing…, Not having read… (nunca don't knowing). Podemos conservar una conjunción para mayor claridad: after / before / while / since / when + -ing y when / if / unless / once / although + participio pasado: When asked…, If left untreated…, Once completed… Tras after y before (preposiciones) va -ing, nunca to.
explain.en: Negative: not + participle. Keep a conjunction for clarity: after / while + -ing, when / if / once + past participle.

examples.en: Not having received a reply, I sent a second email.
examples.es: Al no haber recibido respuesta, envié un segundo correo.

examples.en: When asked about the merger, the CEO declined to comment.
examples.es: Cuando le preguntaron por la fusión, el consejero delegado declinó hacer comentarios.

examples.en: If left untreated, the infection can spread quickly.
examples.es: Si no se trata, la infección puede extenderse rápidamente.

examples.en: After signing the contract, both parties shook hands.
examples.es: Tras firmar el contrato, ambas partes se dieron la mano.

explain.title: 6 · Relativas reducidas
explain.es: Podemos eliminar who / which / that (+ be) y dejar solo el participio: the man (who is) sitting there, the files (which were) sent today, anyone wishing to attend (= who wishes). -ing = activo; -ed = pasivo. Límite importante: -ing no sirve para una acción puntual ya terminada: The man who stole my bag (no The man stealing my bag, salvo que la acción esté en curso).
explain.en: Drop who / which (+ be): the man sitting there, the files sent today. Don't use -ing for a single completed past action.
formula: Nombre + *participio pasado* + … (pasiva: = who / which is / was …)

examples.en: Passengers travelling to Paris should go to Gate 12.
examples.es: Los pasajeros que viajen a París deben dirigirse a la puerta 12.

examples.en: The proposals submitted last week will be reviewed by the committee.
examples.es: El comité revisará las propuestas presentadas la semana pasada.

examples.en: Anyone wishing to attend the seminar should register online.
examples.es: Quien desee asistir al seminario debe inscribirse en línea.

explain.title: 7 · Dangling participles
explain.es: Un dangling participle (participio «colgante») es un participio cuyo sujeto implícito no coincide con el de la principal. El resultado es ilógico o cómico: Walking home, the rain started (¿la lluvia caminaba?). Solución: cambia el sujeto de la principal o usa una oración completa. Si el participio tiene otro sujeto, nómbralo (formal): The weather being fine, we ate outside · With prices rising… Excepción: fórmulas fijas como generally speaking, judging by, considering, all things considered.
explain.en: The implied subject of the participle must be the subject of the main clause. Otherwise, rewrite or name the subject (with prices rising…).

examples.en: Arriving at the hotel, the room was not ready. → Arriving at the hotel, we found that the room was not ready.
examples.es: Al llegar al hotel, vimos que la habitación no estaba lista.

examples.en: With interest rates rising, many families are struggling to pay their mortgages.
examples.es: Con los tipos de interés subiendo, muchas familias tienen dificultades para pagar la hipoteca.

examples.en: All things considered, the conference was a success.
examples.es: Teniéndolo todo en cuenta, el congreso fue un éxito.

explain.title: Oración completa frente a participial
explain.es: Las dos versiones significan lo mismo. La participial es más compacta y formal (informes, noticias, essays); la oración completa es más clara y natural en la conversación.
explain.en: Same meaning: the participle clause is more compact and formal; the full clause is more natural in speech.

explain.title: ¿Cómo reduzco una oración?
explain.title_en: How do I reduce a clause?

items.es: Comprueba que las dos oraciones tienen el mismo sujeto. Si no, no reduzcas (o usa with + sujeto).
items.en: Check that both clauses have the same subject.

items.es: Quita el conector (because, when, as…) y el sujeto de la subordinada.
items.en: Remove the conjunction and the subject.

items.es: ¿Activa (simultánea o causa)? → -ing. ¿Pasiva? → participio pasado. ¿Anterior y terminada? → having + participio.
items.en: Active → -ing; passive → past participle; earlier → having + past participle.

items.es: ¿Negativa? → not delante. ¿Hace falta claridad? → conserva after, while, when, if.
items.en: Negative → not. Keep a conjunction if needed.

items.es: Pon una coma y relee: ¿quién hace la acción del participio? Debe ser el sujeto que va justo después de la coma.
items.en: Add a comma and check who does the action.

lines.en: Good evening. Hit by the worst floods in fifty years, the north of the country is on high alert tonight.
lines.es: Buenas noches. Golpeado por las peores inundaciones en cincuenta años, el norte del país está esta noche en alerta máxima.

lines.en: After three days of non-stop rain, the river burst its banks this morning, flooding hundreds of homes.
lines.es: Tras tres días de lluvia ininterrumpida, el río se desbordó esta mañana e inundó cientos de viviendas.

lines.en: Families living near the river have been evacuated, and several roads remain closed, causing long delays.
lines.es: Las familias que viven cerca del río han sido evacuadas y varias carreteras siguen cortadas, lo que provoca largos retrasos.

lines.en: Is there any sign of improvement?
Judging by the latest forecast, yes. Asked about the clean-up, the mayor said it would take months.
lines.es: A juzgar por la última previsión, sí. Preguntado por la limpieza, el alcalde dijo que llevaría meses.

explain.title: Truco del sujeto
explain.es: Antes de escribir una participial, pregúntate «¿quién hace esto?». La respuesta tiene que ser el sujeto que va justo después de la coma: Walking home, I… ✓ / Walking home, the rain… ✗. Recuerda: -ing = hace (activo), -ed = le hacen (pasivo), having + participio = ya lo había hecho. Registro: brillan en informes, noticias y essays; al hablar, because / when suenan más naturales.
explain.en: Ask «who does this?»: the answer must be the subject right after the comma. -ing = active, -ed = passive, having + past participle = before. Formal writing, not casual speech.

exercises.en: Complete the second sentence so that it means the same as the first. Use the key word and 3-6 words.

items.q:
Because she didn't have enough money, she couldn't buy the flat. 🔑 HAVING
Not _____, she couldn't buy the flat.
items.a: having enough money

items.q:
After he had checked the figures, he signed the report. 🔑 HAVING
_____, he signed the report.
items.a: Having checked the figures

items.q:
The castle, which was built in 1450, is open to the public. 🔑 BUILT
The castle, _____, is open to the public.
items.a: built in 1450

items.q:
The fire destroyed the warehouse, so 50 people lost their jobs. 🔑 LEAVING
The fire destroyed the warehouse, _____ jobs.
items.a: leaving 50 people without

items.q:
When the minister was asked about the scandal, she said nothing. 🔑 ASKED
_____ the scandal, the minister said nothing.
items.a: When asked about

items.q:
People who live near the airport complain about the noise. 🔑 LIVING
People _____ complain about the noise.
items.a: living near the airport

items.q:
As I didn't know the city, I got lost. 🔑 KNOWING
_____, I got lost.
items.a: Not knowing the city

items.q:
If you store it in the fridge, the sauce will last a week. 🔑 STORED
_____, the sauce will last a week.
items.a: (If) stored in the fridge

items.q:
Since we had been warned about the traffic, we left early. 🔑 BEEN
Having _____ the traffic, we left early.
items.a: been warned about

items.q:
While I was waiting for the train, I called my mother. 🔑 WAITING
_____ the train, I called my mother.
items.a: While waiting for

exercises.title: Traduce al inglés
exercises.en: Translate into English using a participle clause.

items.q: Al llegar a la oficina, vi que la puerta estaba abierta.
items.a: Arriving (On arriving) at the office, I saw that the door was open.

items.q: Construida en 1900, la estación es hoy un museo.
items.a: Built in 1900, the station is now a museum.

items.q: Tras terminar la reunión, nos fuimos a comer.
a: Having finished the meeting, we went for lunch.
After finishing the meeting, we went for lunch.

items.q: Como no sabía la respuesta, no dije nada.
items.a: Not knowing the answer, I said nothing.

items.q: Los pasajeros que viajen a Londres deben embarcar ahora.
items.a: Passengers travelling to London should board now.

items.q: Si se usa correctamente, esta herramienta es muy segura.
items.a: Used correctly, this tool is very safe.

items.q: La empresa cerró su fábrica y dejó a 200 personas sin trabajo.
items.a: The company closed its factory, leaving 200 people out of work.

items.q: Cuando le preguntaron por su futuro, el entrenador sonrió.
items.a: When asked (Asked) about his future, the coach smiled.

items.q: Con los precios subiendo, mucha gente ahorra menos.
items.a: With prices rising, many people are saving less.

items.q: Tras haber sido rechazado tres veces, por fin consiguió el trabajo.
items.a: Having been rejected three times, he finally got the job.

exercises.title: Lee y contesta
exercises.es: Lee la noticia. Marca T o F y contesta las preguntas.
exercises.en: Read the news article. Tick T or F and answer the questions.
text: Built in 1882 and badly damaged by a fire in 2019, the Northbridge Covered Market reopened yesterday after a three-year restoration. Having raised over £12 million from public and private sources, the city council was able to restore the building's original iron structure and stained-glass windows.

Thousands of visitors queued from early morning, causing long delays in the city centre. Stallholders, many of them from families that have worked there for generations, were delighted. "Not knowing whether the market would ever reopen, we spent three very difficult years," said Ana Ruiz, whose fish stall was opened by her grandfather.

Asked about the cost of the project, the mayor said it had been worth every penny. "Restored with care and run by local people, this market is the heart of our city," she said. Visitors wishing to take a guided tour can book online.

items.q: The market was built after the fire of 2019.
The restoration took three years.
The large number of visitors caused delays in the city centre.
items.why: …queued from early morning, causing long delays…

items.q: Why were the last three years difficult for the stallholders?
items.a: Because they didn't know whether the market would ever reopen.

items.q: Who opened Ana Ruiz's fish stall?
items.a: Her grandfather.

items.q: Rewrite with a full clause: "Asked about the cost of the project, the mayor said…"
items.a: When the mayor was asked about the cost of the project, she said it had been worth every penny.

items.q: Find a reduced relative clause in the last paragraph.
items.a: Visitors wishing to take a guided tour (= who wish to take a guided tour).

items.q: Find a perfect participle clause in paragraph 1.
items.a: Having raised over £12 million from public and private sources

exercises.title: Ahora escribe tú
exercises.es: Escribe frases propias en registro formal o periodístico.
exercises.en: Write your own sentences in a formal or journalistic style.

items.q: Describe un edificio de tu ciudad empezando con un participio pasado (Built in…, Designed by…).
items.a: Ej.: Designed by Gaudí, Casa Batlló is one of the most visited buildings in Barcelona.

items.q: Cuenta lo que hiciste después de terminar algo, con Having + participio.
items.a: Ej.: Having finished my exams, I went on holiday to Portugal.

items.q: Explica una decisión con Not + -ing.
items.a: Ej.: Not wanting to miss the deadline, I worked all weekend.

items.q: Escribe un titular con una participial de resultado (…, causing / leaving…).
items.a: Ej.: Heavy snow closed the airport, leaving thousands of passengers stranded.

items.q: Escribe un aviso formal con una relativa reducida (Anyone wishing…, Passengers travelling…).
items.a: Ej.: Anyone wishing to attend the conference should register before 1 May.

checklist.es: Uso -ing para acciones simultáneas, causas y resultados.
checklist.en: I use -ing for time, reason and result.

checklist.es: Uso el participio pasado con sentido pasivo: Built in…, Used correctly…
checklist.en: I use past participles with a passive meaning.

checklist.es: Uso having + participio para una acción anterior.
checklist.en: I use having + past participle for an earlier action.

checklist.es: Hago la negativa con not y uso after / while / when + participio.
checklist.en: I can form negatives and use conjunction + participle.

checklist.es: Reduzco relativas: the people living here, the files sent today.
Evito los dangling participles: mismo sujeto en las dos partes.
